description: The pie chart presents the distribution of articles across media outlets, showing 18 labeled slices with numeric values printed inside each wedge and outlet names placed around the perimeter (no separate legend is shown, and no slices appear exploded or otherwise emphasized). The largest slice is labeled “Breitbart,” colored blue, with a value of 14, followed by “Other,” colored gray, with a value of 13. Two medium-sized slices labeled “Drudge Report” (orange) and “The Daily Caller” (green) each show 8, and “The Huffington Post” (red) shows 7. Two similarly sized slices labeled “NPR” (purple) and “Vox” (brown) each show 6, while “The Guardian” (pink) and “BBC” (light gray) each show 5, and “RT” (yellow‑green) shows 4. The remaining nine slices each show 3 and appear as small wedges, labeled (with distinct colors) “National Review,” “Daily Kos,” “Daily Mail,” “Redstate,” “Fox News,” “CNN,” “PoliticusUSA,” “Shareblue,” and one additional small 3-valued wedge among these; visually, the two largest wedges (“Breitbart” and “Other”) are adjacent, with many of the 3-valued slices grouped together in one region of the chart.
